collection_metadata.locality: Pitchandikulam Forest, Auroville, Tamil Nadu, India

stem_bark.text: The bark of Majidea zanguebarica is greyish-coloured, rough, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Majidea zanguebarica is greyish-coloured, rough, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.

seed.text: The seeds of Majidea zanguebarica are subglobose, less than 1 cm in diameter, black-coloured and velvety.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Majidea zanguebarica are subglobose, less than 1 cm in diameter, black-coloured and velvety.

fruit.text: The fruit of Majidea zanguebarica is a 3-lobed capsule. The fruit is 3 cm long and wide with an apical beak and it is yellow-pinkish-coloured. The ripe fruits split, exposing the bright red interior, with 3 spherical velvety black seeds.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Majidea zanguebarica is a 3-lobed capsule. The fruit is 3 cm long and wide with an apical beak and it is yellow-pinkish-coloured.
The ripe fruits split, exposing the bright red interior, with 3 spherical velvety black seeds.

flower.text: The flowers of Majidea zanguebarica are grouped in terminal panicles. The calyx is composed of 5 sepals. The sepals are 7 mm long and 4 mm wide and lanceolate. The calyx is light green and finely tomentose. The corolla is composed of 4 pink-coloured petals. The petals are oblong and clawed, 5 mm long and 2.5 mm wide. The androecium is composed of 8 stamens. The filaments are about 1 cm long and the anthers are 1 mm long. The style is very short with a simple stigma . The ovary is 3-celled. The buds are covered with short and white hairs.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Majidea zanguebarica are grouped in terminal panicles.
The calyx is composed of 5 sepals. The sepals are 7 mm long and 4 mm wide and lanceolate. The calyx is light green and finely tomentose.
The corolla is composed of 4 pink-coloured petals. The petals are oblong and clawed, 5 mm long and 2.5 mm wide.
The androecium is composed of 8 stamens. The filaments are about 1 cm long and the anthers are 1 mm long.
The style is very short with a simple stigma.
The ovary is 3-celled.
The buds are covered with short and white hairs.

leaf.text: The leaves of Majidea zanguebarica grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is compound, imparipinnate with a 3 cm long petiole. The leaflets are bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaflet is coriaceous and glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the midrib beneath). The leaves have a very short petiolule . The leaflet of Majidea zanguebarica is 4-5 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate to lanceolate, the apex is obtuse and slightly retuse, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Majidea zanguebarica is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 5-6 m high.
habit.text_html: Majidea zanguebarica is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 5-6 m high.

distribution.text: In India, Majidea zanguebarica is a naturalized exotic species which is planted along the roads and cultivated in parks and gardens for its evergreen foliage, showy flowers and fruits. Majidea zanguebarica is native to eastern Africa and it is found throughout the tropics in cultivation.
distribution.text_html:
• Ecology :

    In India, Majidea zanguebarica is a naturalized exotic species which is planted along the roads and cultivated in parks and gardens for its evergreen foliage, showy flowers and fruits.

  • Distribution :

    Majidea zanguebarica is native to eastern Africa and it is found throughout the tropics in cultivation.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Majidea zanguebarica is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Majidea zanguebarica is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Majidea zanguebarica is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Majidea zanguebarica is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.

phenology.text: From May to September. From August to November. From August to November. Evergreen foliage. ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )

reforestation.text: Majidea zanguebarica is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species prefers full sun but can withstand moderate shade. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Majidea zanguebarica is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. 
    The species prefers full sun but can withstand moderate shade.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
